messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: [P2] HarborCloud (hc-092) private VPC — intermittent inbound healthcheck failures observed on NLB target group -> 503/504s. Paging oncall-network.

oncall-network-nick: Got it, pinging in. Pulling up alerts and NLB target health now.

netops-alyssa: NLB target group shows flapping healthchecks since 06:22 UTC, spike in backend connection resets from NAT subnet (10.2.3.0/24). Target 10.2.3.17 returns 504 occasionally. No obvious errors from backend app yet.

se-raj: Lina (cust) reported API ingestion latency and failed webhooks ~06:20. They're seeing elevated 5xx from our edge hostname: harbor.harborcloud.internal.

eng-sre-maya: Reproducing a direct healthcheck locally from a jump host:
```
curl -v --resolve harbor.harborcloud.internal:443:10.2.3.17 https://harbor.harborcloud.internal/health
* Connected to 10.2.3.17 (10.2.3.17) port 443 (#0)
> GET /health HTTP/1.1\n> Host: harbor.harborcloud.internal\n\n< HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable\n```
So backend sometimes returns 503. Need to rule out SNAT/conntrack exhaustion first.

netops-alyssa: Checked node conntrack and iptables counters: TIME_WAIT/conntrack entries high on nodes serving NAT. ipvs stats show high retries. Could be ephemeral port exhaustion during bursts.

eng-sre-maya: Suggest temporary mitigation: shift a portion of traffic away from the NLB to the ALB pool in the private subnet (ALB targets are healthy). Lower DNS TTL to 30s and change route weight to ALB 30% -> 70% NLB to reduce pressure while we dig.

oncall-network-nick: Agreed. I'll prepare the DNS weight change and adjust SGs to ensure ALB can accept the redirect. Also will open a cloud support ticket for potential NAT gateway port exhaustion.

cust-ops-lina: Messaging HarborCloud now: inform them of partial traffic shift and potential short-term latency. ETA for initial mitigation: 10–15m.

netops-alyssa: Executing quick checks on healthcheck source IPs and SGs. NLB healthchecks originate from 10.1.0.0/24 in their account; target SG blocks some ephemeral ranges. Updating SG to allow healthcheck + ephemeral src ports for 1 hour.

eng-sre-maya: Rolling restart of the agent on 10.2.3.17 to clear conntrack/worker threads. Command: `systemctl restart harbor-agent` — will monitor.

se-raj: HarborCloud confirms they can tolerate partial shift. Request they keep low TTL on their external DNS as well for 10m to allow rapid rollback.

infra-nick: Opened ticket with cloud provider (ticket #CP-90712) — initial response indicates NAT gateway port exhaustion is possible; asked for source metrics.

oncall-network-nick: Performed weighted DNS update: ALB weight now 40%, NLB 60%. TTL set to 30s. Monitoring traffic delta and 5xx rates.

incident-bot: Metric alert: 5xx rate down 45% over last 5m after weighted shift (alert suppressed).

netops-alyssa: After SG tweak and agent restart, target 10.2.3.17 health stabilized. Conntrack entries decreasing. Still seeing periodic small spikes but within normal.

eng-sre-maya: Leaving a mitigation runbook note: if reoccurs -> fully drain NLB (weight 0) and route 100% to ALB; ensure ALB session affinity and stickiness configured for short timeouts.

cust-ops-lina: HarborCloud accepts the current partial shift; they're OK with us keeping them posted every 20m.

oncall-network-nick: Preparing handoff: I'll stay on for another 30m then hand to night oncall Tom. Current state: traffic split 40/60, TTL 30s, SG temporary rule in place (expires +1h), cloud ticket open. Monitoring shows error-rate within SLO for 20m.

oncall-night-tom: Acknowledged, will take over at 1735130000. Please leave the DNS weight and SG notes in the channel.

pm-lina: Logged incident in tracker INC-2025-089 (HarborCloud VPC NLB health flapping). Assigned follow-up action: investigate NAT gateway scaling and suggest longer term: private NAT autoscaling or egress proxy pool.

incident-bot: NOTE: Remember to rotate temporary SG changes and revert DNS weights once stable for 30m.

oncall-network-nick: Reverting plan if green for 60m: restore default SG and move DNS back to NLB 100% during scheduled maintenance window.

eng-sre-maya: Leave monitoring hooks: set anomaly alert to 2xx/5xx ratio and conntrack count threshold. Added a dashboard link to the incident ticket.

cust-ops-lina: HarborCloud says incoming webhooks resumed, no data loss reported. Thanks team.

oncall-night-tom: Took the handoff at 1735130000. I'll keep an eye till 1735133600 then close unless new alerts.

incident-bot: RESOLUTION TRACKING: mitigation in place, customer impact reduced. Close after 60m stable and postmortem assigned.
